statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, r is characterized as follows. If there exists an index j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] > 0, then r is the sum of all integers v such that 1 <= v <= 100 and v occurs in nums (each distinct positive value is counted exactly once). Otherwise, when no element of nums is positive, r is the maximum of the set {nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums)}.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: max_sum(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, -100 <= r <= 5050.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, r >= max_{0 <= i < len(nums)} nums[i].
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, r <= sum_{0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] > 0} nums[i], where this sum counts positive elements with multiplicity and is 0 if no element is positive.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_k for some k >= 0 such that 0 <= i_0, i_k < len(nums), the values nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_k] are pairwise distinct, and r = nums[i_0] + nums[i_1] + ... + nums[i_k].
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, for every k >= 0 and every sequence of indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_k with 0 <= i_0 and i_k < len(nums) such that nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_k] are pairwise distinct, the sum nums[i_0] + nums[i_1] + ... + nums[i_k] is <= r.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: If max_sum(nums) returns r and max_sum(other) returns s, then r = s.
preconditions: nums and other are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers, each with length between 1 and 100 and every element between -100 and 100. For every integer v, v occurs in nums if and only if v occurs in other.

statement: If max_sum(nums) returns r and max_sum(xs) returns s, then r = s.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), and nums contains at least one positive element. Let xs be the slice obtained by deleting from nums every element nums[i] with nums[i] <= 0, preserving order.

statement: If max_sum(xs) returns r and max_sum(ys) returns s, then s = r + v.
preconditions: xs is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(xs) <= 99 and -100 <= xs[i] <= 100 for every i with 0 <= i < len(xs), xs contains at least one positive element, v is an integer with 1 <= v <= 100, v does not occur in xs, and ys is the slice obtained by appending v to xs.
